title: Siri AI Is Finally About to Understand Your Health Checkup Data, but Apple Has Locked It in Beta

content_html:
The most awkward weak spot in Apple's AI assistant is quietly being patched. On November 11, source @itspdfu revealed on X that in the just-released first developer preview beta of iOS 27.3, Apple has planted a feature toggle for Siri AI that lets it read the "Health" app—though for now all of them are turned off.

92 Types of Data, From Activity Rings to Sleep, All in One Query

This toggle, codenamed "IF / HealthSearch," is meant to connect health information to Siri's "Find" tool. Its search range covers 92 HealthKit data types, and it can look up both recent records and historical summaries. Activity rings, individual workouts and summaries, sleep summaries, medication schedules, and the "Health Age" and health assessments in the new Health app are all fair game. The list also includes "Readiness" (readiness status), but "Vitals" (vital signs) is nowhere to be seen. Another toggle, "IF / HealthSnippets," is responsible for visualizing the results, so health stats, rings, workouts, and sleep can all be displayed visually in dedicated styles.
